docs.title: Cobblestone
docs.text: Server-side navigation for Minecraft.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Cobblestone runs an A* search over the live world and renders the resulting route as a particle trail. Routes account for walking, swimming, climbing, falling, boats, horses, doors, and portals. If the player leaves the route, it is recomputed.

Cobblestone does not teleport players itself. Integrations can register teleport commands, such as EssentialsX /home or Towny /town spawn, as route steps that the player is prompted to run.

/loc set home                   # save the current position
/nav home                       # navigate back to it

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["/navigate <destination>"] --> B[Destination providers]
    B --> C[A* search]
    D[Search modifications] --> C
    C --> E[Path]
    E --> F[Trip]
    F --> G[Navigator]
    G -. player strays .-> C

Destination providers, search modifications, and navigators are all extensible. See the developer documentation.

docs.title: Supported versions
docs.text:
Platform Minecraft Java Paper 26.1+ 25+ Sponge 1.21.1 21+ Sponge 26.1+ 25+

Each release supports the latest Minecraft version. Older Minecraft versions are not supported, with one exception: Sponge 1.21.1 has long-term support, shipped as its own jar named Cobblestone-Sponge-1.21.1-<version>.jar.

docs.title: Performance
docs.text: Searches run asynchronously and are bounded per player. The configuration file exposes options to increase or reduce the resources each search may use.

docs.title: Benchmarking
docs.text:
Stonebrick runs the search against terrain captured from a real Minecraft world, without a server, and reports what each route cost. Runs are deterministic, so a number that moves means the algorithm changed. How it is built is in project/stonebrick/README.md.

File in project/stonebrick/data/ What Committed scenarios.yml routes: a start and a destination yes agents.yml loadouts: what the player can do (walk, fly, boat, no pickaxe) yes corpus.yml the world seed and the pinned Paper build yes needed-chunks.yml how much terrain each route needs yes captures/ the captured terrain no, generate it

Every scenario runs under every loadout that applies to it.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
You need the JDKs from Contributing, including JDK 25, which runs the Paper server. Gradle finds the JDKs installed on your machine.

Generate the terrain once:

cd project
./gradlew captureCorpus -PacceptMinecraftEula=true

This downloads the Paper build pinned in corpus.yml, checks it against the checksum pinned there, generates the seeded world, and captures what each scenario needs. It only captures what is missing, so it is safe to re-run. The flag records that you accept the Minecraft EULA; nothing starts without it.

Captures of the same seed differ in small decorations, so your numbers will not match a teammate's exactly. Captures and baselines therefore stay on your machine.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
./gradlew :stonebrick:stonebrick-bench:run --args="<command> [options]"
Command What it does list Show the scenarios and loadouts run Run everything and compare against your baselines; fails if a gated metric moved accept Run everything and record the results as your baselines sweep Run at several heuristic weights and print nodes against path cost check Say whether a scenario can be benchmarked: each heuristic's result, and Dijkstra's optimum path Print the cells of the route each loadout's search found verify-regions Compare the region estimate with the true cost along each route

A first run has no baselines, and prints each result's outcome, expansions and path cost. That is the current state of the search.

To check the region estimate itself, run its suite. It takes a minute or two and uses at most half your memory and processors:

./gradlew verifyRegions

To measure a change, record a baseline before it and compare after:

git checkout main
./gradlew :stonebrick:stonebrick-bench:run --args="accept"
git checkout my-change
./gradlew :stonebrick:stonebrick-bench:run --args="run"
Status Meaning MATCH within tolerance CHANGED a gated metric moved; review it, then accept if intended CONFIGURATION the baseline measured different settings or a different capture; re-accept DEGENERATE the search left the captured terrain; see below

Gated metrics are path cost, time and steps, nodes opened and expanded, chunk reads, and simulated time. Wall time and heap are reported but never fail a run.

Option Effect --scenario overworld/ocean one route --tag surface routes with a tag --agent flyer one loadout --heuristic zero Dijkstra: slow, but finds the optimal path --weight 2.0, --weights 1,1.5,2 heuristic weight(s) --io spinning simulated disk: zero, nvme, sata, spinning, busy --baselines <dir> keep baselines elsewhere

docs.title: Adding a scenario
docs.text:
The utility plugin (project/stonebrick/utility, /stonebrick or /sb) picks and checks scenarios on a server running the seeded world.

  1. Find the ends. /sb probe <x> <z> says where a body stands in a column and which structures are there; /sb pieces <x> <z> lists a structure's pieces with a place to stand in each; /sb find <block> <x> <z> finds blocks such as _bed or bookshelf; /sb span <biome> <x> <y> <z> finds a straight line that stays inside a biome.
  2. Mark them: /sb mark <name> origin and /sb mark <name> dest where you stand, or give coordinates (surface for a Y stands on the ground there). The scenario is tagged by where its ends are; change that with /sb tag <name> <tags>. For a destination that is an area, add box: { from: {...}, to: {...} } to its destination by hand.
  3. /sb check <name> (add --generate on a world that may generate chunks). It captures the terrain, widening the capture until every route that arrives stays inside it, runs each heuristic under each loadout and Dijkstra, and reports how each did: the cost, how close a failed run came, and how far each is from the optimum. A scenario is unusable only when the terrain its routes need cannot be captured; a heuristic failing is a result, not a reason.
  4. Copy the scenario's entries from the plugin's out/scenarios.yml and out/needed-chunks.yml into scenarios.yml and needed-chunks.yml, run captureCorpus, and commit both files.

docs.title: Adding a heuristic
docs.text: Add a value to SearchSettings.Heuristic, build it in MinecraftHeuristics.forPlayer, and add the matching value to the bench's Scenario.Heuristic. Paper, Sponge and the bench all build heuristics there. Compare with sweep --heuristic <name>: a curve across weights, not a single point.

docs.title: Players
docs.text:
Cobblestone computes a route to a destination and draws it as a particle trail. No client modifications are required.

Command Alias Purpose /navigate /nav Navigate to a destination, or open the navigation menu. /location /loc Save, remove, and list locations. /cobblestone /stone Manage trips. Also holds navigate and location as subcommands.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Save your current position:

/loc set home

Navigate back to it from anywhere:

/nav home

Cobblestone reports Searching for a route..., then Success! once a route is found. Hover over Success! to see the search time and estimated travel time. Hover over Searching for a route..., or over the error if no route is found, to see the destination's address. For a fixed place, such as a saved location, your death location or a set of coordinates, the coordinates are shown too, so you can still find your way there by hand. The trip ends automatically when you arrive within two blocks of the destination.

docs.title: The trail
docs.text:
The trail renders only the next segment of the route, brightest at the point to head for next.

  • Straying. If you leave the trail, a short guide path is drawn back to it. Beyond 32 blocks (by default), the route is recomputed from your current position.
  • Action steps. Some steps require an action: opening a door, placing a boat, mounting a horse, entering a portal, or running a command. Cobblestone highlights the location and sends a message. Command prompts, such as Run /warp market., can be clicked.
  • Ending. A trip ends on arrival, on /stone cancel, or on disconnect. Death does not end a trip. A trip to a pet or mount ends if it dies, and a trip to a player ends if they log off.

docs.title: The navigation menu
docs.text:
Type /nav on its own to open a menu of everywhere you can go. /nav -help lists the flags /nav takes. On a server with the Geyser integration, Bedrock players can open the menu without typing by doing the Simple Clap emote.

  • Items marked » open a further list. Others start navigating as soon as you click them.
  • Something that is both a place and a list opens, and lists the place itself first.
  • A destination that needs more from you, such as coordinates block, asks for it before starting: in a form on Paper, or as a command to finish in chat on Sponge.
  • A destination you cannot go to right now, such as death before you have died, turns into a barrier that says why. Click it again to try again.
  • The top row of the first page shows the destinations you went to most recently, so a favorite is one click away. They are forgotten when the server restarts.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text: Type /nav and press Tab to list the destinations available to you. The list depends on the plugins installed on the server.

docs.title: Saved locations
docs.text:
/nav home                          # a personal location
/nav location private home         # the same, fully qualified
/nav location global spawn         # a server-wide location

docs.title: Death location
docs.text:
/nav death

Your most recent death location. Admins may disable this destination. If you have not died since it was enabled, you are told so.

docs.title: Respawn point
docs.text:
/nav respawn

Where you will respawn: your bed, a charged respawn anchor, or a point set by /spawnpoint. If you have none, you are told so.

docs.title: World spawn
docs.text:
/nav spawn

Where you respawn if you have no respawn point of your own. The server has one, normally in the overworld.

docs.title: Surface
docs.text:
/nav surface

The nearest place open to the sky. The route heads upward, so it is the quickest way out of a cave or a mine. Water, leaves and glass count as a roof. If you are already open to the sky, you are told so instead.

docs.title: Target
docs.text:
/nav target

The block you are looking at, up to 256 blocks away: the open space in front of it, or the ground below that if it is the side of a wall. Water counts as something to look at, unless you are underwater; grass and flowers are looked through.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
/nav coordinates block 100 64 -200                 # a block in this world
/nav coordinates block 100 64 -200 world_nether    # a block in another world
/nav coordinates surface 100 -200                  # the open-sky spot at x=100, z=-200

Whole numbers only. The world is optional and defaults to the one you are in. Tab completion offers your own coordinates. The word coordinates is always required, so /nav surface still means the nearest open sky. Coordinates in terrain that has never been generated are refused.

docs.title: Mount
docs.text:
/nav mount
/nav horse

The tamed horse, donkey, mule, llama or camel you last rode. horse is another name for it, for any of these. The route is recomputed periodically as it moves while it is loaded, and otherwise heads to where it was last seen. If it dies, the trip ends, and there is no mount to go back to until you ride another.

docs.title: Pets
docs.text:
/nav pet Rex

Your named, tamed animals that are currently loaded. Pets that share a name are numbered by when they were tamed: Rex, Rex-2, … The route is recomputed periodically as the pet moves, and the trip ends if the pet dies.

docs.title: Players
docs.text:
/nav player Steve

Online players only. The route is recomputed periodically as the target moves, and the trip ends if they log off.

docs.title: Worlds
docs.text:
/nav world world_nether

Routes through a known entry point, typically a portal that Cobblestone has observed in use.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Available only when the corresponding integration is installed:

/nav town riverwood home           # Towny: town spawn
/nav town riverwood outpost north  # Towny: outpost
/nav npc Blacksmith                # Citizens: NPC
/nav home cabin                    # EssentialsX: home
/nav spawn                         # EssentialsX: spawn
/nav quest lostlantern             # Quests, BeautyQuests: current objective
/nav compass tower                 # BetonQuest: quest compass target

docs.title: Addresses
docs.text:
Every destination has a full address, such as cobblestone location private home. Leading words may be omitted as long as the remainder identifies exactly one destination:

/nav cobblestone location private home
/nav location home
/nav home

The destination's own name is always required. Some levels, such as town and NPC names, are marked strict by their provider and are also required. A destination that takes values, such as coordinates, takes them after its name; they are never part of the address.

If the input matches more than one destination, the candidates are listed:

That destination is ambiguous; be more specific: location private home, essentials home home

Tab completion is suppressed when there are too many candidates. Type a few more characters and press Tab again.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flags follow the destination and may be combined.

Flag Effect -live / -no-live Enable or disable periodic route recomputation. Enabled by default only for moving targets. -no-<mode> Exclude a travel mode, e.g. -no-swim. -no-mode <mode> Long form of the above. -no-world <world> Exclude a world, e.g. minecraft:the_nether. -no-dimension <dimension> Exclude a dimension, e.g. the_end. -navigator <id> Select a navigator. The default is trail.

Travel modes: walk, swim, fly, mine, fall, climb, boat, horse, door. The fly mode is used only if you are able to fly, and mine only where you may break blocks.

/nav home -no-swim -no-mine
/nav player Steve -no-live
/nav home -no-world minecraft:the_nether

docs.title: Saved locations
docs.text:
/loc set <name>      # save the current position
/loc unset <name>    # delete a location
/loc list            # list personal and global locations

/loc is short for /location, which is also available as /cobblestone location. Names are single words and are scoped to each player. Where a personal and a global location share a name, use location private <name> or location global <name>.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text:
Up to three trips may run at once by default.

/stone trips              # list active trips
/stone cancel <id>        # cancel one trip
/stone cancel all         # cancel all trips and pending searches
/stone hud [on|off]       # show or hide your trip HUD

/stone cancel with no argument is equivalent to all.

While you have trips, a HUD on the right of the screen lists each one with its estimated time left, updated every second:

Trips
home - 3m 24s
caves - 48s

Each trip is named by the shortest part of its address that tells it apart from your other trips. /stone hud with no argument switches it on or off; your choice is remembered.

To tell several trails apart, stand still for a second: a few blocks ahead of you, the name of each trip appears over its trail (or the guide back to it), named the same way as in the HUD. With one trip to a player named Steve it reads Steve; add a trip to a town also named Steve and they read player Steve and town Steve. A label only appears where you can see it, and the labels go away as soon as you move, so they stay out of your way while you follow the trail. Hit the red Cancel above a label to cancel that trip; it works from any distance you can see it from. On Sponge servers, other players nearby can see your labels too, but only you can cancel your trips with them.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Message Cause There is no route to that destination. No traversable route exists. The search ran out of resources before finding a route. The search reached its cell limit. The search took too long and was stopped. The search reached its time limit. No destination matches ... No destination has that name. That destination is ambiguous; be more specific: ... Add a word from the full address. Usage: /navigate ... The destination takes values; type them as shown. ... is not valid there. Usage: /navigate ... One of the values could not be read. You already have too many active trips; cancel one first. Cancel a trip with /stone cancel. You don't have permission to do that. The destination or navigator is restricted.

Search limits are set by the server. See Configuration.

docs.title: Core
docs.text:
• Personal and server-wide saved locations.
  • Navigation to a player's death location, to other players, and to other worlds.
  • Nether and End portal links, learned by observing players use them.
/loc set home
/loc set spawn -global
/nav death

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Companion plugins add destinations, register teleport commands as route steps, and apply third-party build protection to routes.

Integration Adds Towny Towns, outposts, and plots; /town spawn and /nation spawn as route steps; build protection. EssentialsX Homes and spawn; /home and /spawn as route steps. Citizens NPCs. BetonQuest, BeautyQuests, Quests (PikaMug), Quests (LMBishop) Quest objectives, with optional automatic trips. Typewriter A Navigate Player action.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
Player nodes default to allow; admin nodes default to op.

Node Default Grants cobblestone.navigate allow /navigate, /cobblestone trips, /cobblestone cancel cobblestone.location allow Personal locations cobblestone.hud allow Showing or hiding one's own trip HUD cobblestone.navigator allow Non-default navigators cobblestone.admin.location.global op Global locations cobblestone.admin.reload op /cobblestone reload cobblestone.admin.portals op /cobblestone portals clear cobblestone.admin.regions op /cobblestone regions clear cobblestone.admin.loglevel op /cobblestone loglevel

Each destination also has its own node, derived from its address. For example, to prevent a group from navigating to other players:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.player.* false

See Permissions.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text: Pathfinding runs asynchronously. World reads and calls into other plugins, such as Towny build checks, run on the main thread. See search.max_concurrent_per_player and search.algorithm.* in Configuration.

docs.title: Chunk loading
docs.text: By default, searches may load chunks that have already been generated. Terrain generation is disabled unless search.chunks.policy is set to allow_load_and_generate, which permanently enlarges world files. See Configuration.

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Saved locations, the most recent death location of each player, and learned portal links are stored in an embedded H2 database. Learned portal links can be cleared with /cobblestone portals clear.

The terrain regions behind the REGIONS heuristic are kept on disk, a few kilobytes per chunk that searches have touched. A world's can be cleared with /cobblestone regions clear <world>. See Configuration.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Everything lives under /cobblestone. The two commands players use most are also registered on their own, so the short forms are all a player needs:

/loc set home     # save the current position
/nav home         # navigate back to it
/loc list         # list saved locations

All of these behave identically on Paper and Sponge.

Command Aliases /cobblestone /stone /cobblestone navigate /navigate, /nav /cobblestone location /location, /loc, /cobblestone loc

docs.title: /cobblestone navigate [destination…] [flags]
docs.text:
Usually typed as /nav; /navigate and /cobblestone navigate are the same command.

Permission: cobblestone.navigate (default allow) · Players only

Resolves the destination, runs a search, and starts a trip if a route is found. With no arguments, opens the navigation menu instead. /nav -help lists the flags.

docs.title: Destination
docs.text:
One or more words identifying a node in the destination tree. Each provider contributes a branch keyed by the name of the plugin that registered it:

cobblestone location private home
cobblestone location global spawn
cobblestone death
cobblestone respawn
cobblestone spawn
cobblestone surface
cobblestone target
cobblestone coordinates block <x> <y> <z> [world]
cobblestone coordinates surface <x> <z> [world]
cobblestone player <name>
cobblestone world <name>
towny town <town> home
citizens npc <name>
essentials home <name>

Leading words may be omitted if the remainder is unambiguous (/nav home). The final word and any level marked strict by its provider are always required. Ambiguous input is rejected with a list of candidates. Matching is case-insensitive.

docs.title: Flags
docs.text:
Flag Argument Effect -navigator navigator id Display style. Default trail. Gated by cobblestone.navigator.<id>. -no-mode mode word Exclude a travel mode from the search. -no-<mode> — Shorthand: -no-fly, -no-boat, -no-mine, … -no-world world key Exclude a world from routing. Repeatable. -no-dimension dimension Exclude a dimension from routing. Repeatable. -live — Force the trip to re-search periodically. -no-live — Force it not to.

Mode words: walk, swim, fly, mine, fall, climb, boat, horse, door.

Trips to moving destinations (players) are live by default; all others are not. A live trip re-searches every trips.live_interval_ticks and yields to search.max_concurrent_per_player. A manual /navigate takes priority over a live re-search.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
/nav home
/nav town riverwood home -no-mine
/nav player Steve -no-live
/nav location global spawn -no-dimension the_nether
