docs.title: /cobblestone
docs.text: Prints help. All subcommands are also available under /stone.

docs.title: /cobblestone location set <name> [-global]
docs.text:
/location and /loc are shorthand for /cobblestone location.

Permission: cobblestone.location; -global additionally needs cobblestone.admin.location.global · Players only

Saves the caller's current block position under name. Personal by default; -global makes it available to all players.

/loc set home
/loc set spawn -global

Names are single words. Personal names are scoped per player. A personal and a global location may share a name; they are distinguished by address (location private home, location global home).

docs.title: /cobblestone location unset <name> [-global]
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.location; -global needs cobblestone.admin.location.global

Removes a personal location, or a global location with -global.

docs.title: /cobblestone location list
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.location · Players only

Lists the caller's personal locations and all global locations.

Locations (3):
home - minecraft:overworld 128, 71, -344
mine - minecraft:overworld 210, 12, -400
spawn - minecraft:overworld 0, 64, 0 (global)

docs.title: /cobblestone trips
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.navigate · Players only

Lists the caller's active trips with id, destination, and estimated remaining time.

Active trips (2):
[1] location private home - 2 minutes and 10 seconds
[2] towny town riverwood home - 48 seconds

docs.title: /cobblestone hud [on|off]
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.hud · Players only

Shows or hides the caller's trip HUD; with no argument, switches it. The choice is stored and survives reconnects. While the caller has trips, the HUD lists each one with its estimated remaining time, refreshed every second:

Trips
private home - 2m 10s
riverwood home - 48s

A trip from /navigate is named by the fewest words of its address that tell it apart from the caller's other trips. A trip started by another plugin shows the label that plugin gave it.

If trips.hud is off, the command reports that the HUD is turned off on the server.

docs.title: /cobblestone cancel [<id>|all]
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.navigate · Players only

Cancels a trip by id. With all or no argument, cancels all trips and pending searches.

docs.title: /cobblestone reload
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.admin.reload

Reloads config.yml. Live settings apply immediately. Changes to restart-only settings are reported and not applied:

Cobblestone configuration reloaded.
Some settings changed but need a server restart to apply: data.backend, search.chunks.policy

docs.title: /cobblestone portals clear
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.admin.portals

Deletes all learned portal links. Links are relearned as players use portals.

Cleared 42 discovered portal transitions.

docs.title: /cobblestone regions clear <world>
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.admin.regions

Deletes a world's region cache, in memory and on disk. Searches build the regions again as they need them. Use it after changing the world's terrain in a way Cobblestone cannot see: editing it offline, with WorldEdit or /fill, or trimming chunks to be generated again.

Cleared the regions of minecraft:overworld; they are built again as searches need them.

docs.title: /cobblestone loglevel <level>
docs.text:
Permission: cobblestone.admin.loglevel

Sets Cobblestone's console log level until restart: trace, debug, info, warn, or error.

At debug, each search logs its outcome, step count, and timing.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
config.yml is generated on first run, with a comment above each setting.

PaperSponge

plugins/cobblestone/config.yml

config/cobblestone/config.yml

/cobblestone reload reloads the file. Settings marked live apply immediately; settings marked restart apply on the next server start.

Each platform generates its own settings. Unrecognized settings are reported on startup and ignored.

docs.title: locale
docs.text:
Setting Default locale.default en restart

Language for console and system messages, as a BCP 47 tag (en, en-US, fr). Player messages use the client's language when a translation is available.

docs.title: messages
docs.text:
Setting Default messages.show_prefix true live

Prepends the [✦] prefix to player messages.

docs.title: data
docs.text:
Setting Default Values data.backend H2 H2 restart data.file cobblestone any name restart

Storage for saved locations, death locations, and portal links. data.file is the database file name, without extension, in the plugin's data folder.

docs.title: trips
docs.text:
Setting Default trips.max_active_per_player 3 live trips.live_interval_ticks 100 live trips.recalculate_distance 32 live trips.hud true live trips.holograms true live
  • max_active_per_player: Maximum concurrent trips per player.
  • live_interval_ticks: Interval between re-searches for live trips. Live re-searches are the main recurring cost; increase this before reducing search limits.
  • recalculate_distance: Distance in blocks a player may stray before the route is recomputed. Below this distance, a guide path back to the trail is drawn instead. 0 disables recomputation.
  • hud: Shows each player's active trips in a HUD with the time left on each. Players can hide it for themselves with /cobblestone hud off. While shown, a player is given a scoreboard of their own, so they do not see the server's main scoreboard (its sidebar, or teams it uses for name colors). Turn this off if another plugin relies on that. It is never shown on Folia, which has no scoreboard API.
  • holograms: Floats a label naming each trip over its trail (or the guide back to it), a few blocks ahead of the player, once they have stood still for a second; the labels go away as soon as they move. Hitting the red Cancel above a label cancels its trip, from any distance. This is the default; a plugin starting a trip can turn its label on or off. Labels are entities. On Paper they are seen only by their player and never saved. On Sponge, whose API can't hide an entity from other players, everyone nearby sees them (only the owner's hit does anything); any left behind by a crash are removed when their chunk loads.

docs.title: search
docs.text:
Setting Default search.max_concurrent_per_player 1 restart

Maximum concurrent searches per player, including live re-searches. Live re-searches yield to this limit; a manual /navigate always runs.

docs.title: search.algorithm
docs.text:
Setting Default search.algorithm.max_cells_visited 200000 live search.algorithm.max_wall_clock_seconds 60 live search.algorithm.heuristic RUNNING_AVERAGE live search.algorithm.heuristic_weight 1.5 live search.algorithm.tier1_unsolved_pessimism 1.5 live search.algorithm.running_average_width 5 live
  • max_cells_visited: Cell limit per search. Memory use is a few hundred bytes per cell, so the default peaks in the tens of megabytes. Increase for longer routes; decrease on small heaps.
  • max_wall_clock_seconds: Time limit per search.
  • heuristic: How the search estimates the rest of a route. REGIONS reads the connected patches of terrain ahead, finding better routes and handling water, caves and boats, at the cost of extra chunk reads per search. RUNNING_AVERAGE extrapolates from the last few steps; it is cheaper but never routes a player onto the water by boat.
  • heuristic_weight: Deprecated. The A* heuristic weight for RUNNING_AVERAGE only; REGIONS reads search.regions.heuristic_weight. 1.0 yields optimal routes; higher values search faster with routes at most this factor longer than optimal.
  • tier1_unsolved_pessimism: Cost multiplier for route legs that have not yet been solved. 1.0 disables it.
  • running_average_width: Window size of the running-average heuristic.

docs.title: search.chunks
docs.text:
Setting Default Values search.chunks.policy allow_load loaded_only, allow_load, allow_load_and_generate restart
  • loaded_only: Read only chunks already in memory. Lowest cost; searches frequently fail where terrain is unloaded.
  • allow_load: Also read generated chunks from disk. Recommended.
  • allow_load_and_generate: Also generate new terrain. World files grow permanently.
PaperSponge

Paper can read an unloaded chunk without loading it, so allow_load is inexpensive.

Sponge must load a chunk to read it. Cobblestone acquires a chunk ticket, copies the chunk, and releases the ticket immediately.

Setting Default search.chunks.max_load_requests 256 live

Maximum chunk tickets held at once. Values below about 64 disable read-ahead and slow searches.

docs.title: search.regions
docs.text:
The REGIONS heuristic cuts the world into regions of terrain once, a 16-block cube at a time, and shares them between every search until a block in that cube changes.

Setting Default search.regions.persist true restart search.regions.memory 128 restart search.regions.flush_period 60 restart search.regions.heuristic_weight 1.7 live
  • persist: Keep regions on disk, so a restart does not start from nothing: under plugins/Cobblestone/regions/ on Paper and cobblestone/regions/ in the server folder on Sponge, a folder per world by its key, as the world's own data is kept: minecraft:the_nether in regions/minecraft/the_nether/. A few kilobytes per chunk's worth of terrain, only where searches went. A world's regions are built again from scratch if its seed or height changes.
  • memory: Memory each world's regions may use, in megabytes, least recently used dropped first and read back from disk when needed. The terrain within about 70 blocks of each navigating player is kept on top of this until their trip ends, so the searches that re-plan around them stay fast.
  • flush_period: How often new regions are written, in seconds. They are also written when a world saves and when the server stops. A write touches only the regions that changed.
  • heuristic_weight: A* heuristic weight under REGIONS. 1.0 yields optimal routes; higher values search faster with routes at most this factor longer than optimal. The region estimate runs close to the true cost, so it bears a higher weight than the running average.

Block changes made while the server is running are tracked: a changed cube's regions are dropped about 10 seconds after the change, together with any further changes in that time, and built again when a search next needs them. Changes Cobblestone cannot see are not tracked: edits made while the server is stopped, edits by tools that set blocks without block events (such as WorldEdit or /fill), and chunks trimmed or deleted to be generated again. After those, clear the world's regions with /cobblestone regions clear <world>.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Symptom Adjustment Long routes fail with "ran out of resources" or "took too long" Increase max_cells_visited and max_wall_clock_seconds. Ensure search.chunks.policy is at least allow_load. High CPU usage Increase trips.live_interval_ticks, keep search.max_concurrent_per_player at 1, and decrease max_cells_visited. On Sponge, decrease search.chunks.max_load_requests. High memory usage Decrease max_cells_visited. Searches must not load chunks Set search.chunks.policy to loaded_only.

Use /cobblestone loglevel debug to log the timing of each search.

docs.title: portals
docs.text:
Portal destinations are not exposed by the server API, so Cobblestone learns portal links by observing players.

Setting Default portals.discovery true live portals.cost_seconds 5.0 live portals.normalize_entry true live portals.normalize_exit true live
  • discovery: Learn new portal links. Existing links remain in use when disabled.
  • cost_seconds: Assumed cost of a portal traversal.
  • normalize_entry: Treat any entry into a nether portal as entering at its center, so each portal has a single destination. Required for reliable portal routing.
  • normalize_exit: Place the player at the center of the destination portal, at ground level.

Clear learned links with /cobblestone portals clear.

docs.title: deaths
docs.text:
Setting Default deaths.track true live

Records each player's most recent death location and offers the death destination. When disabled, recording stops and the destination is hidden; stored data is retained. To restrict it by group instead, use cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.death.

docs.title: menu
docs.text:
Setting Default menu.title <#4AA8FF>Navigation Menu live menu.filler minecraft:gray_stained_glass_pane live menu.recents true live menu.icons.<name> see below live

The navigation menu opens when a player types /navigate with no destination. It is a double chest with a border, which holds the back, page and close buttons. Inside it are four rows of destinations. On the first page, the top row is the player's recent destinations instead, followed by a gap. Entries are listed alphabetically. A level with only one way on is skipped.

  • title: The menu's title, in MiniMessage.
  • filler: The item in the border and the gap.
  • recents: Whether to show recent destinations. They are kept in memory until restart.

Items are written as an item key, such as minecraft:oak_sign, or as head: followed by a skin texture value, as head databases such as minecraft-heads.com publish them.

menu.icons sets the items for Cobblestone's own entries (death, spawn, player, …), the buttons (back, page, close, breadcrumb), and the fallbacks for entries that choose none (destination, folder). Each integration sets its own items in its own config. Other players always show their own heads, and pets show their spawn egg.

A destination that needs more input, such as coordinates block, asks for it before navigating: in a dialog on Paper, and on Sponge by handing the player the command to finish in chat.

docs.title: metrics
docs.text:
Setting Default metrics.enabled true restart

Anonymous usage data via bStats. bStats can also be disabled globally in its own configuration.

docs.title: navigators.trail
docs.text:
Setting Default navigators.trail.buffer_cells 256 live navigators.trail.particles [TRAIL] live navigators.trail.highlight_particles [END_ROD] live navigators.trail.colors [FFFFFF, 4AA8FF] live navigators.trail.density 0.2 live navigators.trail.particle_ticks 10 live
  • buffer_cells: Length of the rendered path segment ahead of the player.
  • particles: Particle types, chosen at random per particle. TRAIL and DUST use colors; other types render as-is. A TRAIL particle drifts along the trail and lasts exactly particle_ticks, so the trail stays crisp ahead of a moving player. On a server too old to have TRAIL (before 1.21.2, such as Sponge for 1.21.1), DUST is drawn in its place. Particles requiring other data are not supported.
  • highlight_particles: Particles at highlighted points, such as action steps.
  • colors: TRAIL and DUST colors as RRGGBB, chosen at random per particle.
  • density: Mean particles per cell per tick. Fractional values are probabilities: 0.7 means a 70% chance of one particle per cell per tick.
  • particle_ticks: How long each TRAIL particle lasts. Shorter is crisper on the move; longer is fuller. Each particle drifts in a straight line at about a block a second, so beyond about 40 ticks it visibly strays off a curving trail.

Particle names follow the server's particle registry.

docs.title: Integrations
docs.text:
Each integration is a separate plugin, available on Modrinth. An integration requires both Cobblestone and its target plugin, and disables itself if the target is absent.

The integrations listed here are Paper builds.

Integration destinations are registered under the target plugin's name. Permission nodes therefore take the form cobblestone.navigate.towny.…, not cobblestone.navigate.cobblestonetowny.…. See Permissions.

docs.title: Towny
docs.text:
CobblestoneTowny · requires Towny

/nav town <town> home            # town spawn
/nav town <town> outpost <name>
/nav town <town> plot <name>     # named plot
/nav town <town> type <name>     # plots by type (shop, farm, …)
/nav resident                    # the player's own town

The town level is strict: /nav town riverwood home is valid; /nav riverwood home is not.

  • Teleport route steps. /town spawn, /nation spawn, and /town outpost are offered as route steps when the player is permitted to use them under Towny's rules.
  • Build protection. Routes do not mine through blocks the player may not break.
  • Menu items. In the navigation menu each town shows as a banner in its map color (/town set mapcolor), matched to the nearest dye. Change the items under icons in plugins/CobblestoneTowny/config.yml.

docs.title: EssentialsX
docs.text:
CobblestoneEssentials · requires EssentialsX; EssentialsSpawn optional

/nav home <name>     # an Essentials home
/nav spawn           # server spawn (requires EssentialsSpawn)

/home and /spawn are offered as route steps when the player is permitted to use them.

Change how homes and the spawn look in the navigation menu under icons in plugins/CobblestoneEssentials/config.yml.

docs.title: Geyser
docs.text:
CobblestoneGeyser · requires Geyser on this server

Bedrock players open the navigation menu by performing an emote, instead of typing /nav. The emote runs /navigate as the player, so it needs the same permission. The default emote is Simple Clap, one of the four every Bedrock player starts with; change the list of emote ids under emotes in plugins/CobblestoneGeyser/config.yml.

Geyser must run on this server: Geyser on a proxy cannot report emotes to it.

Note

Bedrock players see textured heads in the menu as plain heads unless the texture is also listed in Geyser's custom-skulls.yml.

docs.title: Citizens
docs.text:
CobblestoneCitizens · requires Citizens

/nav npc <name>

NPC positions are resolved at search time. The npc level is strict.

docs.title: BetonQuest
docs.text:
CobblestoneBetonQuest · requires BetonQuest · GPL-3.0

/nav compass <name>

Each active quest compass is a destination. Setting a compass target can start a trip automatically.

plugins/CobblestoneBetonQuest/config.yml:

auto-navigate: true      # start a trip when a compass target is set
navigator: trail
particles: [DUST, GLOW]
colors: [FFD54F, 4FC3F7]
compasses:               # per-compass overrides, keyed by compass id
  dungeon_entrance:
    enabled: false

This module links against BetonQuest and is licensed under GPL-3.0.

docs.title: BeautyQuests
docs.text:
CobblestoneBeautyQuests · requires BeautyQuests

/nav quest <name>

The current locatable stage of each started quest is a destination. Advancing to a locatable stage can start a trip automatically.

plugins/CobblestoneBeautyQuests/config.yml (per-quest overrides keyed by numeric quest id):

auto-navigate: true
navigator: trail
quests:
  '3':
    enabled: false

docs.title: Quests (PikaMug)
docs.text:
CobblestonePikamugQuests · requires Quests

/nav quest <name>

Current objectives are destinations, with the same automatic trip behavior. Per-quest overrides are keyed by quest id:

quests:
  slay-the-dragon:
    enabled: false

The plugin is named Quests, so its nodes take the form cobblestone.navigate.quests.quest.<name>.

docs.title: Quests (LMBishop)
docs.text:
CobblestoneBishopQuests · requires Quests

/nav quest <id>

Each started quest with a position task still to reach is a destination. Tracking a quest starts a trip to that position. Per-quest overrides are keyed by quest id:

quests:
  citizen1:
    enabled: false

The plugin is named Quests, so its nodes take the form cobblestone.navigate.quests.quest.<id>.

docs.title: Typewriter
docs.text:
cobblestone-typewriter · Typewriter extension

Adds a Navigate Player action entry, which starts a trip for the triggering player to a configured location. Install it as a Typewriter extension, not in plugins/.

docs.title: Name collisions
docs.text: Multiple integrations may offer the same name, such as home. Destinations remain distinct by full address (essentials home cabin, towny town riverwood home). Ambiguous player input is rejected with a list of candidates.

docs.title: Custom integrations
docs.text: All integration functionality is available through the public API. See the developer documentation.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text: Cobblestone defines a fixed set of command nodes and generates a node for every destination and navigator.

docs.title: Command nodes
docs.text:
Node Default Grants cobblestone.navigate allow /navigate, /cobblestone trips, /cobblestone cancel cobblestone.location allow /location set/unset/list for personal locations cobblestone.hud allow /cobblestone hud cobblestone.navigator allow Parent of the per-navigator nodes cobblestone.admin.location.global op Creating and deleting global locations cobblestone.admin.reload op /cobblestone reload cobblestone.admin.portals op /cobblestone portals clear cobblestone.admin.regions op /cobblestone regions clear cobblestone.admin.loglevel op /cobblestone loglevel PaperSponge

Declared in paper-plugin.yml with the defaults above.

Registered with the permission service on startup. Player nodes are assigned to the USER role and admin nodes to the ADMIN role.

docs.title: Destination nodes
docs.text:
Each destination has a canonical address, which maps to a node under cobblestone.navigate:

Address Node cobblestone location private home cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.location.private.home cobblestone death cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.death cobblestone respawn cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.respawn cobblestone spawn cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.spawn cobblestone surface cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.surface cobblestone target cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.target cobblestone coordinates block cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.coordinates.block cobblestone coordinates surface cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.coordinates.surface cobblestone mount cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.mount cobblestone pet Rex cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.pet.Rex cobblestone player Steve cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.player.Steve towny town riverwood home cobblestone.navigate.towny.town.riverwood.home citizens npc Blacksmith cobblestone.navigate.citizens.npc.Blacksmith

Values typed after a destination are not part of its address, so /nav coordinates block 100 64 -200 checks cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.coordinates.block whatever the coordinates are.

The first segment is the lower-cased name of the owning plugin. Integrations register under the plugin they integrate with (towny, citizens, essentials, betonquest, …), not under the name of the companion plugin.

docs.title: Evaluation
docs.text:
• Default allow. A destination is permitted unless its node is explicitly set to false.

  • Exact node only. Parent nodes are not consulted, so denying cobblestone.navigate.towny has no effect. Deny a branch with a wildcard that your permission plugin expands:

    /lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.towny.* false

    The permission plugin's own precedence rules apply, so a narrower grant overrides a broader deny.

  • Tab completion. Denied destinations are omitted from suggestions.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Deny navigation to players:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.player.* false

Deny the death destination except for one group:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.death false
/lp group donor permission set cobblestone.navigate.cobblestone.death true

Deny a single town:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.towny.town.riverwood.* false

Deny all Citizens NPCs except one:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.citizens.* false
/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigate.citizens.npc.Blacksmith true

docs.title: Navigation and teleportation
docs.text: Destination nodes control only whether a player may be routed to a destination. Teleport commands such as /home, /town spawn, and /warp remain governed by their own plugins' permissions. Integrations offer a teleport as a route step only when the player may run the command.

docs.title: Provider permissions
docs.text: A provider may attach additional required permissions to a destination (DestinationLeaf#permissions). The player must hold all of them. Cobblestone's own destinations declare none.

docs.title: Navigator nodes
docs.text:
Non-default navigators are gated by cobblestone.navigator.<id>:

/lp group default permission set cobblestone.navigator.guide false

These nodes default to allow and are checked only when -navigator <id> is used. The default trail navigator requires only cobblestone.navigate.

docs.title: Case sensitivity
docs.text: Destination keys are used verbatim as node segments (…citizens.npc.Blacksmith). If a deny has no effect, try the lower-cased form; not all permission plugins fold case consistently.

docs.title: Developers
docs.text:
Task Page Register destinations Destinations Start a trip for a player Trips Add teleports and other transitions to searches Search modification Restrict where searches may break or pass Search modification Render routes with a custom navigator Navigators Run a search and read the path Searching

Platform-specific code blocks are tabbed. Selecting Paper or Sponge applies site-wide.

docs.title: Dependency
docs.text:
Two artifacts are published per platform:

  • …-api: The navigation library: searches and search modifications.
  • …-plugin-api: Plugin features: destinations, navigators, and trips. Includes …-api transitively.

Most integrations should depend on …-plugin-api.

PaperSponge build.gradle.kts
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    // Provided at runtime by the Cobblestone plugin — never shade it.
    compileOnly("org.cobblestonemc:paper-plugin-api:0.1.0")
}
pom.xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.cobblestonemc</groupId>
  <artifactId>paper-plugin-api</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <scope>provided</scope>
</dependency>

Declare the dependency so that Cobblestone loads first:

paper-plugin.yml
dependencies:
  server:
    cobblestone:
      load: BEFORE
build.gradle.kts
repositories {
    mavenCentral()
}

dependencies {
    // Provided at runtime by the Cobblestone plugin — never shade it.
    compileOnly("org.cobblestonemc:sponge-plugin-api:0.1.0")
}
pom.xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>org.cobblestonemc</groupId>
  <artifactId>sponge-plugin-api</artifactId>
  <version>0.1.0</version>
  <scope>provided</scope>
</dependency>

Declare the dependency so that Cobblestone loads first:

META-INF/sponge_plugins.json
"dependencies": [
  { "id": "cobblestone", "load-order": "after", "optional": false }
]

Do not shade the API

The API is provided at runtime by the Cobblestone plugin. A shaded copy causes ClassCastExceptions across class loaders.

Latest version: . The API is pre-1.0 and may change between minor versions.

docs.title: Services
docs.text:
Services are accessed through two static entry points:

PaperSponge 
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.api.CobblestoneCoreApi;
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.plugin.api.CobblestonePaperApi;

// …-api: the navigation library
NavigationService navigation = CobblestoneCoreApi.navigationService();
SearchModificationRegistrar searches = CobblestoneCoreApi.registrar();

// …-plugin-api: destinations, navigators, trips
IntegrationRegistrar integrations = CobblestonePaperApi.registrar();
TripService trips = CobblestonePaperApi.tripService();

Both query Bukkit's ServicesManager. Call them from onEnable() or later, not from a constructor.

import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.api.CobblestoneCoreApi;
import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.plugin.api.CobblestoneSpongeApi;

// …-api: the navigation library
NavigationService navigation = CobblestoneCoreApi.navigationService();
SearchModificationRegistrar searches = CobblestoneCoreApi.registrar();

// …-plugin-api: destinations, navigators, trips
IntegrationRegistrar integrations = CobblestoneSpongeApi.registrar();
TripService trips = CobblestoneSpongeApi.tripService();

Cobblestone populates these holders during its ConstructPluginEvent. Access them from StartingEngineEvent or later.

Naming

The Paper accessor is CobblestonePaperApi; the Sponge accessor is CobblestoneSpongeApi. The names will be aligned in a future major version.

docs.title: Ownership
docs.text:
Every registration has an owner plugin. Registrations are removed when the owner disables. The owner's name also determines the destination branch and its permission nodes.

PaperSponge 
CobblestonePaperApi.registrar().registerDestinations(this, new MyDestinations());

Passing this registers destinations under your plugin's lower-cased name.

An integration for another plugin should pass that plugin, so that the address is town riverwood home rather than cobblestonetowny town riverwood home:

Plugin towny = getServer().getPluginManager().getPlugin("Towny");
CobblestonePaperApi.registrar().registerDestinations(towny, new TownyDestinations());

CobblestoneSpongeApi.registrar().registerDestinations(container, new MyDestinations());

Passing your PluginContainer registers destinations under your plugin's lower-cased id.

An integration for another plugin should pass that plugin's container, so that the address is town riverwood home rather than cobblestonetowny town riverwood home:

PluginContainer towny = Sponge.pluginManager().plugin("towny").orElseThrow();
CobblestoneSpongeApi.registrar().registerDestinations(towny, new TownyDestinations());

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    subgraph you["Your plugin"]
        DS[DestinationService]
        SMS[SearchModificationService]
        NF[NavigatorFactory]
        CALL[Direct call]
    end

    DS -->|IntegrationRegistrar| NAV["/navigate"]
    NF -->|IntegrationRegistrar| TRIP[Trip]
    SMS -->|SearchModificationRegistrar| SEARCH[Search]
    NAV --> SEARCH
    SEARCH -->|Path| TRIP
    CALL -->|TripService| TRIP
    CALL -->|NavigationService| SEARCH
  • Destination: A named location that players can navigate to.
  • Search: Computes a Path from a player to a destination.
  • Search modification: Adds transitions and restricts which blocks may be broken or entered.
  • Trip: A path being followed by a player, ticked by Cobblestone.
  • Navigator: Renders a trip.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text:
• SearchHandle.future() completes on a Cobblestone thread. Return to the main thread (or region thread on Folia) before accessing server state.
  • computeTransitions, computeBreakChecker, and computePassChecker run once per search on the calling thread, normally the main thread.
  • The returned checkers run during the search, possibly off the main thread, and return a CompletableFuture. Checks that require the main thread must schedule work there and complete the future.
  • Checkers are invoked thousands of times per search. Return completed futures where possible and cache results per search.

docs.title: Destinations
docs.text: A destination is a named location that /navigate can route to. Destinations are supplied by a DestinationService, which is queried per player, per search.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[DestinationService] -->|provide player| B[DestinationTree]
    B --> C[entries, by key]
    C -->|a destination| D[DestinationLeaf]
    C -->|a subtree| B
    D --> E[MinecraftDestination]
    E --> F["regions() — where it actually is"]

A tree is a set of entries, each named by a key. An entry is a destination, a subtree of further entries, or both — a town is somewhere to go, and also holds its home and plots. A tree itself is never a destination; only its entries are.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
A single destination at a fixed location:

PaperSponge 
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.plugin.api.CobblestonePaperApi;
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.plugin.api.Destination;
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.plugin.api.DestinationService;

public final class ShopsPlugin extends JavaPlugin {
  @Override
  public void onEnable() {
    CobblestonePaperApi.registrar().registerDestinations(this, player ->
        Destination.tree()
            .destination("market", () -> Destination.at(marketLocation(), "Market"))
            .build());
  }
}

import net.kyori.adventure.text.Component;
import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.plugin.api.CobblestoneSpongeApi;
import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.plugin.api.Destination;
import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.plugin.api.DestinationService;

@Listener
public void onStartedEngine(StartedEngineEvent<Server> event) {
  CobblestoneSpongeApi.registrar().registerDestinations(container, player ->
      Destination.tree()
          .destination("market", () -> Destination.at(marketLocation(), Component.text("Market")))
          .build());
}

For a plugin named Shops, the address is shops market. Players may use /nav market, or /nav shops market if the name is ambiguous.

Note

The tree is already registered under the owner plugin's name. Do not add a top-level entry for it.

docs.title: Trees
docs.text:
Destination.tree() begins a tree. Add entries to it, each keyed by a string: destination(key, …) for somewhere to go, subtree(key, …) for a tree of further entries beneath it.

Tip

Hold a tree you are still adding to in a var — var tree = Destination.tree(); — rather than spelling out its type, DestinationTree.Builder<MinecraftDestination<World, Vector3i>>.

PaperSponge 
Destination.tree()
    .subtree("warp", () -> warps(player))
    .subtree("dungeon", Destination.tree()
        .strict()                                     // (1)!
        .destination("crypt", () -> Destination.at(crypt, "The Crypt"))
        .destination("mines", () -> Destination.at(mines, "Deep Mines")))
    .build();
  1. A strict tree's key cannot be omitted: /nav dungeon crypt is valid; /nav crypt is not.
Destination.tree()
    .subtree("warp", () -> warps(player))
    .subtree("dungeon", Destination.tree()
        .strict()                                     // (1)!
        .destination("crypt", () -> Destination.at(crypt, Component.text("The Crypt")))
        .destination("mines", () -> Destination.at(mines, Component.text("Deep Mines"))))
    .build();
  1. A strict tree's key cannot be omitted: /nav dungeon crypt is valid; /nav crypt is not.

Rules:

  • Keys are single tokens. Upper case is permitted; special characters are not. Spaces are permitted but discouraged, since keys appear in commands and permission nodes.
  • Each key is added once. Adding a key again, or a key that is already an alias, throws.
  • Subtrees from a supplier are built each time they are traversed, and never if they are not. A subtree given as a builder is built once, when it is added.
  • Return null from provide when there are no destinations for the player. Empty trees are omitted.
  • Mark large trees strict(). Strict trees are skipped when computing suggestions.
  • alias(other, key) lets a destination answer to another name players may guess. An alias is never suggested, and the destination keeps its own key in messages and permissions.

docs.title: Both at once
docs.text:
An entry may be a destination and hold a subtree. Build it with Destination.entry() and add it with entry(key, …):

for (Town town : towns()) {
  tree.entry(town.name(), Destination.entry()
      .destination(() -> Destination.regions(() -> claims(town), town.name()))
      .subtree(() -> townDetail(town)));       // its home, outposts, plots
}

/nav town riverwood goes to the whole town; /nav town riverwood home goes to its home. An entry must have a destination, a subtree, or both; build() refuses one with neither.

docs.title: Lazy subtrees
Destination types
docs.text:
Destination provides factories for common cases:

PaperSponge 
// A single block. Its coordinates are shown on hover.
Destination.at(location, "Market");

// Anywhere in one region.
Destination.region(BoxWorldRegion.of(corner1, corner2), "The Arena");
Destination.region(BoxWorldRegion.around(center, 8), "Near the well");
Destination.region(WholeWorldRegion.of(world), "The Nether");

// Several regions — the search heads for whichever is cheapest to reach, and
// the supplier is re-evaluated every search, so a moving target stays current.
Destination.regions(() -> town.claims().stream().map(this::toRegion).toList(), "Riverwood");

// A single block. Its coordinates are shown on hover.
Destination.at(location, Component.text("Market"));

// Anywhere in one region.
Destination.region(BoxWorldRegion.of(corner1, corner2), Component.text("The Arena"));
Destination.region(BoxWorldRegion.around(center, 8), Component.text("Near the well"));
Destination.region(WholeWorldRegion.of(world), Component.text("The Nether"));

// Several regions — the search heads for whichever is cheapest to reach, and
// the supplier is re-evaluated every search, so a moving target stays current.
Destination.regions(
    () -> town.claims().stream().map(this::toRegion).toList(), Component.text("Riverwood"));

A destination with no regions is valid and unreachable. Use this when the target is temporarily unavailable, such as when its world is unloaded.

docs.title: Moving targets
docs.text:
Destination.builder takes the same regions as Destination.regions, plus optional settings:

Destination.builder(
        npc.getName(),
        // Re-read on every search, so a live trip follows the NPC.
        () -> npc.isSpawned()
            ? List.of(SingleCellWorldRegion.of(npc.getEntity().getLocation()))
            : List.of())
    .mobile()                                  // trips to it default to -live
    .labeled()                                 // its nameplate already names it
    .existence(() -> CitizensAPI.getNPCRegistry().getById(npc.getId()) != null)
    .detail(Component.text("Wanders the market"))
    .build();
  • mobile() sets the default for live trips. Players may override it with -live or -no-live.
  • labeled() says the destination already shows its name in the world, as an NPC's nameplate does.
  • detail(...) and existence(...) are described under Hover detail and Existence.

You may also implement MinecraftDestination yourself; isMobile(), hasLabel(), detail() and exists() are its defaults to override.

docs.title: Leaves
docs.text:
destination(key, () -> destination) is the common case: a destination with no options or permissions that is always valid. For anything more, pass a DestinationLeaf. A leaf describes itself (its permissions and options) and builds its destination only once a player picks it:

  • Tab completion reads every leaf's description on each keystroke, possibly off the server thread, so the description must be cheap and must not read the world.
  • build(OptionValues) runs once, when the command runs, on the thread that owns the player (their region, on Folia). It may read the world around them. It returns a Validity: the destination, or the reason there is nothing to navigate to right now.
// Always valid, nothing typed after the key; the same as destination(key, () -> ...).
DestinationLeaf.of(() -> Destination.at(market, "Market"));

// May be invalid.
DestinationLeaf.ofValidity(
    () -> town.isOpen()
        ? Validity.valid(Destination.at(town.spawn(), town.name()))
        : Validity.invalid(Component.text("The town is closed.", NamedTextColor.RED)));

// Requires a permission.
DestinationLeaf.of(() -> Destination.at(vault, "Vault")).withPermissions("towns.vault");

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
A leaf may take values typed after its key, such as the coordinates in /nav coordinates block 100 64 -200. Declare them in the order they are typed, and build the destination from what was typed:

DestinationOption<Outpost> outpost =
    DestinationOption.required(
        "outpost",
        partial -> town.outposts().stream().map(Outpost::name).toList(),
        token -> Optional.ofNullable(town.outpost(token)));

tree.destination(
    "outpost",
    DestinationLeaf.withOptions(
        List.of(outpost),
        values -> {
          Outpost chosen = values.get(outpost);
          return Validity.valid(Destination.at(chosen.spawn(), chosen.name()));
        }));
  • Each option reads one word. DestinationOption.integer(name, hint) reads a whole number and suggests hint; required(…) and optional(…) take any suggestion and parsing logic.
  • Required options come first. Optional ones may be left off from the end.
  • Options are never part of the address, so they never affect the destination's permission node and are never promoted past its name.
  • If the words after the name do not fit, the player is shown the usage, such as /navigate outpost <outpost>.

docs.title: Validity
docs.text: When build returns Validity.invalid(reason), the player is shown reason as is, instead of a search starting. The leaf is still offered in tab completion, so the player learns why rather than finding nothing there. Cobblestone's own destinations use it for surface when the player is already in the open, death when no death is on record, respawn when the player has none, and target when they are not looking at a block in range.

docs.title: Hover detail
docs.text: Set detail(...) on the builder to add a line to the hover text of Searching for a route... and of the error that follows if no route is found. The address is always shown; the detail goes beneath it. Cobblestone's own destinations use it for the coordinates of fixed places, such as death, so a player can find the place by hand. Destination.at adds a block's coordinates for you.

docs.title: Existence
docs.text: Set existence(...) on the builder for a target that can stop existing partway through a trip, such as an animal that dies. A trip polls it about once a second and ends quietly once it returns false. Being out of reach, for example unloaded, is not the same as not existing. It is called on the travelling player's thread, so keep it cheap. Cobblestone ends trips to pets and mounts that die, and to players who log off.

docs.title: In the navigation menu
docs.text:
Typing /navigate on its own opens a chest menu of the same tree. By default each entry shows as its key on a plain item. Give it a label, a description and an icon to make it look like yours:

PaperSponge 
tree.entry("riverwood", Destination.entry()
    .destination(() -> wholeTown(riverwood))
    .subtree(() -> townDetail(riverwood))
    .label(Component.text("Riverwood"))
    .description(Component.text("Founded by the river folk"))
    .icon(PaperIcon.of(Material.BLUE_BANNER)));

tree.entry("riverwood", Destination.entry()
    .destination(() -> wholeTown(riverwood))
    .subtree(() -> townDetail(riverwood))
    .label(Component.text("Riverwood"))
    .description(Component.text("Founded by the river folk"))
    .icon(SpongeIcon.of(ItemTypes.BLUE_BANNER.get())));

An Icon is one of:

  • Icon.item("minecraft:oak_sign") — an item, by key.
  • Icon.head(texture) — a player head wearing a skin texture: the base64 textures value that head databases such as minecraft-heads.com publish.
  • Icon.playerHead(uuid) — a player's own head.
  • PaperIcon.of(…) / SpongeIcon.of(…) — a platform item stack, item type, or block, for full control (a custom model, dyed leather, a glint).

Icon.parse(text, fallback) reads head:<texture> or an item key, the form admins write in a config file, and falls back when the text is blank. Read icons from your plugin's own config so admins can theme them.

Your plugin's own entry at the top of the menu is shown with DestinationService.display(player):

public final class ShopsDestinations implements DestinationService {
  @Override
  public DestinationTree<MinecraftDestination<World, Vector3i>> provide(Player player) { … }

  @Override
  public Display display(Player player) {
    return Display.of(Icon.item("minecraft:emerald"));
  }
}

A destination with required options, such as coordinates, asks for them before navigating, using the options' names and suggestions. An option with a handful of suggestions is a choice among them; one with a single suggestion is text that starts as that suggestion.

docs.title: Permissions
docs.text:
• Destination node: cobblestone.navigate.<address>. Generated automatically, default allow, and managed by server admins.
  • A leaf's permissions(): Additional required permissions, all of which the player must hold. Use for access control only. Cobblestone's own destinations declare none.

docs.title: Addressing
docs.text:
Players may omit leading words of an address if the remainder is unambiguous.

  • The final key is always required.
  • strict() trees are always required.
  • Keys that collide across plugins are resolved by the player using the full address.
  • Matching is case-insensitive; quest and Quest collide.

docs.title: Navigators
docs.text: A navigator renders a trip. The built-in trail navigator draws particles along the path. Players select a navigator with -navigator <id>; plugins select one when starting a trip.

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
public interface Navigator<L> {
  void start();                                   // the trip begins
  void tick();                                    // every server tick: render, advance
  void update(Path<L, MinecraftStepPayload> p);   // a re-search replaced the path
  void stop();                                    // arrival, cancellation, or logout
  boolean isComplete();                           // has the player arrived?
  double remainingSeconds();                      // for /cobblestone trips and the HUD

  // Optional:
  default boolean consumeRecalcRequest();              // "I've lost them, re-search"
  default Optional<L> consumeGuideRequest();           // "give me a short path back to the trail"
  default void setGuidePath(Path<L, MinecraftStepPayload> guide);
}

tick() runs every server tick on the player's scheduler (a region task on Folia). It must not block.

The trip ends when isComplete() returns true. Arrival is determined by the navigator; the built-in trail uses a two-block radius.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
An action-bar compass that displays a bearing:

PaperSponge 
final class CompassNavigator implements Navigator<Location> {
  private final Player player;
  private Path<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> path;
  private int step;

  CompassNavigator(Player player, Path<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> path) {
    this.player = player;
    this.path = path;
  }

  @Override public void start() { step = 0; }

  @Override public void tick() {
    if (isComplete() || !player.isOnline()) {
      return;
    }
    Location target = path.steps().get(step).position();
    if (player.getLocation().distanceSquared(target) < 4) {
      step++;
      return;
    }
    player.sendActionBar(Component.text(bearing(player.getLocation(), target)));
  }

  @Override public void update(Path<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> newPath) {
    this.path = newPath;
    this.step = 0;
  }

  @Override public void stop() {
    player.sendActionBar(Component.empty());
  }

  @Override public boolean isComplete() {
    return step >= path.steps().size();
  }

  @Override public double remainingSeconds() {
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = step; i < path.steps().size(); i++) {
      total += path.steps().get(i).time();
    }
    return total;
  }
}

final class CompassNavigator implements Navigator<ServerLocation> {
  private final ServerPlayer player;
  private Path<ServerLocation, MinecraftStepPayload> path;
  private int step;

  CompassNavigator(ServerPlayer player, Path<ServerLocation, MinecraftStepPayload> path) {
    this.player = player;
    this.path = path;
  }

  @Override public void start() { step = 0; }

  @Override public void tick() {
    if (isComplete() || !player.isOnline()) {
      return;
    }
    ServerLocation target = path.steps().get(step).position();
    if (player.position().distanceSquared(target.position()) < 4) {
      step++;
      return;
    }
    player.sendActionBar(Component.text(bearing(player.serverLocation(), target)));
  }

  @Override public void update(Path<ServerLocation, MinecraftStepPayload> newPath) {
    this.path = newPath;
    this.step = 0;
  }

  @Override public void stop() {
    player.sendActionBar(Component.empty());
  }

  @Override public boolean isComplete() {
    return step >= path.steps().size();
  }

  @Override public double remainingSeconds() {
    double total = 0;
    for (int i = step; i < path.steps().size(); i++) {
      total += path.steps().get(i).time();
    }
    return total;
  }
}

docs.title: Registration
Settings
docs.text:
NavigatorSettings carries per-trip overrides. Declare typed keys for the settings your navigator supports:

public final class CompassSettings {
  public static final String NAVIGATOR_ID = "compass";

  public static final NavigatorSettingKey<Boolean> SHOW_DISTANCE =
      new NavigatorSettingKey<>("compass.show_distance");

  public static NavigatorSettings showingDistance(boolean show) {
    return NavigatorSettings.builder(NAVIGATOR_ID).set(SHOW_DISTANCE, show).build();
  }
}

Read them in the factory, falling back to configuration when unset:

boolean showDistance = settings.get(CompassSettings.SHOW_DISTANCE).orElse(config.showDistance());

docs.title: Reading the path
docs.text:
A Path is an origin and an ordered list of Steps. Each step has a position, cost and time in seconds, and a MinecraftStepPayload:

for (Step<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> step : path.steps()) {
  MinecraftStepType type = step.payload().stepType();   // WALK, SWIM, FALL, BOAT, TELEPORT…
  MinecraftInstruction instruction = step.payload().instruction();
}

path.duration() is the estimated travel time; path.cost() is the value minimized by the search.

docs.title: Action steps
docs.text:
OPEN_DOOR, PLACE_BOAT, MOUNT_HORSE, and TELEPORT require player action. MinecraftStepType#isAction() identifies them. A step may also carry an instruction:

if (step.payload().instruction()
    instanceof MinecraftInstruction.CommandInstruction(String command)) {
  // e.g. "/warp market" — make it clickable rather than making them type it.
  player.sendMessage(Component.text("Run " + command)
      .clickEvent(ClickEvent.runCommand(command)));
}

Navigators should notify the player at action steps.

docs.title: Straying
docs.text:
Two optional hooks handle players who leave the route:

  • consumeRecalcRequest(): Return true to re-search from the player's position. The new path is passed to update.
  • consumeGuideRequest(): Return a target to compute a short path from the player to it. The result is passed to setGuidePath.

Both default to no request.

docs.title: Search modification
docs.text:
A SearchModificationService modifies searches through three optional methods:

Method Purpose computeTransitions Adds edges, such as teleports. computeBreakChecker Restricts which blocks may be broken. computePassChecker Restricts which cells may be entered.

Registered services apply to every search:

PaperSponge 
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.api.CobblestoneCoreApi;

CobblestoneCoreApi.registrar().register(this, new WarpModifications(store));

import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.api.CobblestoneCoreApi;

CobblestoneCoreApi.registrar().register(container, new WarpModifications(store));

The registration is removed when the owner disables.

The compute* methods run once per search on the calling thread, normally the main thread. The returned checkers run during the search, possibly off the main thread. See Threading.

docs.title: Transitions
docs.text:
A Transition is an edge from any cell in an origin region to a destination location, at a given cost.

Transition.of(origin, destination, costSeconds, payload);
Transition.of(origin, destination, costSeconds, timeSeconds, payload);
Transition.command(player, destination, costSeconds, "/warp market");
  • origin: A WorldRegion: SingleCellWorldRegion.of(loc), BoxWorldRegion.of(a, b), BoxWorldRegion.around(center, radius), or WholeWorldRegion.of(world).
  • cost: The value minimized by the search, in seconds. time: The travel time reported to the player. Set cost above time to discourage a transition without misreporting its duration.
  • payload: The step type: MinecraftStepPayload.portal(), MinecraftStepPayload.command("/warp market"), or MinecraftStepPayload.of(type).

docs.title: Command transitions
docs.text:
A command can be run from anywhere, so its origin is the player's entire world:

PaperSponge 
@Override
public CompletableFuture<List<Transition>> computeTransitions(Player player) {
  List<Transition> transitions = new ArrayList<>();
  for (Warp warp : store.warps()) {
    if (!player.hasPermission("warps.use." + warp.name())) {
      continue;                                   // (1)!
    }
    transitions.add(Transition.command(
        player, warp.location(), 3.0, "/warp " + warp.name()));
  }
  return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(transitions);
}
  1. Offer a teleport only if the player may use it. Cobblestone does not check teleport permissions.
@Override
public CompletableFuture<List<Transition>> computeTransitions(ServerPlayer player) {
  List<Transition> transitions = new ArrayList<>();
  for (Warp warp : store.warps()) {
    if (!player.hasPermission("warps.use." + warp.name())) {
      continue;                                   // (1)!
    }
    transitions.add(Transition.command(
        player, warp.location(), 3.0, "/warp " + warp.name()));
  }
  return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(transitions);
}
  1. Offer a teleport only if the player may use it. Cobblestone does not check teleport permissions.

docs.title: Portal transitions
docs.text:
A portal pad teleports players on entry, so its origin is the pad's bounding box:

PaperSponge 
BoxWorldRegion pad = BoxWorldRegion.of(padCorner1, padCorner2);
transitions.add(Transition.of(pad, exitLocation, 1.0, MinecraftStepPayload.portal()));

BoxWorldRegion pad = BoxWorldRegion.of(padCorner1, padCorner2);
transitions.add(Transition.of(pad, exitLocation, 1.0, MinecraftStepPayload.portal()));

Omit transitions that are currently unusable, such as those into unloaded worlds.

docs.title: Break checkers
docs.text:
Routes may mine through blocks. A break checker restricts which blocks may be broken; the Towny integration uses one to enforce build protection.

PaperSponge 
@Override
public BreakChecker computeBreakChecker(Player player) {
  // Called once per search: capture what you need here, on the main thread.
  RegionQuery query = worldGuard.createQuery();
  return (p, location, block) -> {
    // Runs during the search, possibly off-thread. Answer without blocking.
    return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(query.testBuild(location, p));
  };
}

The block is supplied lazily (Supplier<BlockData>). Call it only if needed; it may require a chunk lookup.

@Override
public BreakChecker computeBreakChecker(ServerPlayer player) {
  // Called once per search: capture what you need here, on the main thread.
  var claims = claimService.snapshotFor(player);
  return (p, location, block) -> {
    // Runs during the search, possibly off-thread. Answer without blocking.
    return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(claims.mayBreak(location, block));
  };
}

If the check requires the main thread, schedule it and complete the future there:

return (p, location, block) -> {
  CompletableFuture<Boolean> answer = new CompletableFuture<>();
  scheduler.runOnMainThread(() -> answer.complete(protection.canDestroy(p, location)));
  return answer;
};

A search may invoke the checker thousands of times. Cache results per search.

docs.title: Pass checkers
docs.text:
A pass checker restricts which cells the player may enter.

PaperSponge 
@Override
public PassChecker computePassChecker(Player player) {
  boolean vip = player.hasPermission("myserver.vip");
  return (p, location) ->
      CompletableFuture.completedFuture(vip || !vipArea.contains(location));
}

@Override
public PassChecker computePassChecker(ServerPlayer player) {
  boolean vip = player.hasPermission("myserver.vip");
  return (p, location) ->
      CompletableFuture.completedFuture(vip || !vipArea.contains(location));
}

Searches do not route through denied cells.

BreakChecker.ALLOW and PassChecker.ALLOW are the defaults.

docs.title: Example plugin
docs.text: examples/paper-warps implements /warp commands and portal pads with a single SearchModificationService, using only the published API.

docs.title: Searching
docs.text: NavigationService computes a path from a player to a destination. Use it to measure distance, test reachability, or render a path yourself. To guide a player, use Trips instead.

docs.title: Running a search
Regions
docs.text:
To target any cell within a box, pass two opposite corners:

navigationService.navigatePlayerToRegion(player, corner1, corner2);

The search targets the cheapest reachable cell in the box.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
handle.cancel();

Idempotent. If the search is still running, the future completes with FailureReason.CANCELLED. Cancel searches that are no longer needed.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
MinecraftSearchSettings combines algorithm limits with Minecraft-specific exclusions:

MinecraftSearchSettings settings = new MinecraftSearchSettings(
    SearchSettings.builder()
        .maxCellsVisited(50_000)      // cheaper than the server default
        .maxWallClockMillis(5_000L)
        .heuristicWeight(2.0)         // faster, slightly suboptimal
        .build(),
    Set.of(MinecraftStepType.MINE),   // don't route through digging
    Set.of(),                         // excluded world keys
    Set.of("the_nether"));            // excluded dimensions

navigationService.navigatePlayer(player, destination, settings);

MinecraftSearchSettings.defaults() uses library defaults, not the values in config.yml. Short queries, such as reachability checks, should set smaller limits.

Setting Default Meaning maxCellsVisited 200 000 Cell limit; a few hundred bytes per cell maxWallClockMillis 60 000 Time limit heuristic RUNNING_AVERAGE REGIONS reads the terrain ahead; RUNNING_AVERAGE extrapolates from recent steps heuristicWeight the heuristic's own: 1.7 for REGIONS, 1.5 for RUNNING_AVERAGE 1.0 is optimal; higher is faster and bounded-suboptimal tier1UnsolvedPessimism 1.5 Cost multiplier for unsolved route legs runningAverageWidth 5 Heuristic smoothing window

docs.title: Paths
docs.text:
record Path<P, T>(P origin, List<Step<P, T>> steps) { }
record Step<P, T>(P position, double cost, double time, T payload) { }
  • origin: The player's position when the search ran.
  • steps: Positions in order. The last is the destination.
  • cost, time: Per step, not cumulative. path.cost() and path.duration() compute sums; cache the results.
  • payload: A MinecraftStepPayload containing the MinecraftStepType (WALK, SWIM, FLY, MINE, FALL, CLIMB, BOAT, HORSE, OPEN_DOOR, PLACE_BOAT, MOUNT_HORSE, TELEPORT) and an optional MinecraftInstruction.

Paths may cross worlds at TELEPORT steps.

docs.title: Threading
docs.text:
• Call navigatePlayer from the server thread. It returns immediately.
  • The future completes on a Cobblestone worker thread.
  • World data is read on the threads the platform requires; no preloading is needed.

docs.title: Failure reasons
docs.text:
Reason Meaning NO_ROUTE No route connects the origin to the destination. DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE The destination itself is not reachable. LIMIT_EXCEEDED The cell limit was reached. TIMED_OUT The time limit was reached. CANCELLED cancel() was called, or the player disconnected.

LIMIT_EXCEEDED and TIMED_OUT indicate that no route was found within the limits, not that none exists.

docs.title: Trips
docs.text: A trip is a path being followed by a player, rendered by a navigator. Trips recompute when the player strays and end on arrival. TripService starts trips programmatically.

docs.title: Starting a trip
Outcomes
docs.text:
navigate returns a CompletableFuture<TripOutcome>:

tripService.navigate(player, objective, NavigatorSettings.defaults(), "Lost Lantern")
    .thenAccept(outcome -> {
      switch (outcome) {
        case TripOutcome.Started started ->
            log("trip {} started, about {}s", started.tripId(), started.durationSeconds());
        case TripOutcome.Failed failed ->
            player.sendMessage("No route found.");   // failed.reason()
        case TripOutcome.TripLimitReached ignored ->
            player.sendMessage("Finish or cancel a trip first.");
        case TripOutcome.Error error ->
            log.warn("navigation failed", error.throwable());
      }
    });

FailureReason is one of NO_ROUTE, DESTINATION_UNREACHABLE, LIMIT_EXCEEDED, TIMED_OUT, CANCELLED.

An overload accepts only a failure callback:

tripService.navigate(player, objective, NavigatorSettings.defaults(), "Lost Lantern",
    reason -> player.sendMessage("No route: " + reason));

Warning

The future completes off the main thread. Return to the server or region thread before accessing server state.

docs.title: Navigator settings
docs.text:
NavigatorSettings selects the navigator and overrides its appearance for a single trip. Unset values fall back to the server configuration.

PaperSponge 
import org.bukkit.Color;
import org.bukkit.Particle;
import org.cobblestonemc.paper.plugin.api.TrailNavigatorSettings;

NavigatorSettings settings = TrailNavigatorSettings.builder()
    .particles(List.of(Particle.DUST))
    .colors(List.of(Color.fromRGB(0xFFD54F), Color.fromRGB(0x4FC3F7)))
    .highlightParticles(List.of(Particle.END_ROD))
    .showLabel(false) // no floating name over the trail for this trip
    .build();

tripService.navigate(player, objective, settings, "Lost Lantern");

import org.spongepowered.api.effect.particle.ParticleTypes;
import org.spongepowered.api.util.Color;
import org.cobblestonemc.sponge.plugin.api.TrailNavigatorSettings;

NavigatorSettings settings = TrailNavigatorSettings.builder()
    .particles(List.of(ParticleTypes.DUST.get()))
    .colors(List.of(Color.ofRgb(0xFFD54F), Color.ofRgb(0x4FC3F7)))
    .highlightParticles(List.of(ParticleTypes.END_ROD.get()))
    .showLabel(false) // no floating name over the trail for this trip
    .build();

tripService.navigate(player, objective, settings, "Lost Lantern");

showLabel decides whether the trip's name floats over its trail while the player stands still (where hitting Cancel above it cancels the trip). Unset, it follows the server's trips.holograms config.

To use another navigator, build settings for its id:

NavigatorSettings.builder("guide").build();

NavigatorSettings.defaults() selects the server's default navigator with its configured appearance.

docs.title: Starting a trip from a path
docs.text:
To render a path from a search you ran (see Searching):

PaperSponge 
SearchHandle<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> handle =
    CobblestoneCoreApi.navigationService().navigatePlayer(player, destination);

handle.future().thenAccept(result -> {
  if (result instanceof NavigationResult.Success<Location, MinecraftStepPayload> success) {
    CobblestonePaperApi.tripService()
        .startTrip(player, success.path(), NavigatorSettings.defaults(), "Lost Lantern");
  }
});

SearchHandle<ServerLocation, MinecraftStepPayload> handle =
    CobblestoneCoreApi.navigationService().navigatePlayer(player, destination);

handle.future().thenAccept(result -> {
  if (result instanceof NavigationResult.Success<ServerLocation, MinecraftStepPayload> success) {
    CobblestoneSpongeApi.tripService()
        .startTrip(player, success.path(), NavigatorSettings.defaults(), "Lost Lantern");
  }
});

Trips started this way are not live. Use navigate for trips that re-search.

docs.text:
Programmatic trips appear in /cobblestone trips and the trip HUD, count toward trips.max_active_per_player, and can be cancelled by the player. Do not restart a trip the player has cancelled.

Trips end on arrival, cancellation, or disconnect.
